16892:
Compatibility

Manager requires a real RC5 reply on a USB/COM serial port. Detection of a COM port alone does not prove that the SRS ECU is wired to the cable.

Mini MPI, 16-pin OBD socket

MEMS 2J engine K-line: OBD pin 7. RC5/EC5 airbag diagnostic line: OBD pin 13. These are separate circuits.

Adapting a KKL cable

If a KKL interface only reaches pin 7, a suitable diagnostic adapter can route its K line to pin 13 for documented Mini MPI vehicles. Never permanently bridge pins 7 and 13. Verify the actual vehicle and adapter pinouts before modifying the diagnostic lead.

Other models

JDM Minis, MGF, Rover and MG TF variants may use different connectors or SRS controllers. Verify the actual vehicle wiring. No cable has yet been validated on a real RC5 with Manager. Do not touch pyrotechnic airbag or pretensioner wiring. Sources: RoverMEMS and pscan.
16894:
Required cable

The Lucas 5AS uses two separate diagnostic wires rather than a normal single engine K-line. Moving one wire on a standard engine KKL cable is not sufficient.

16-pin OBD socket, applicable vehicles

OBD pin 1: 5AS transmit to tool receive (5AS module C61-24). OBD pin 3: tool transmit to 5AS receive (C61-16). Socket pins are not the same as module connector pins.

Electrical adaptation

5AS signals are approximately 0–12 V, and the 5AS transmit line is inverted. A compatible dual-line interface with level adaptation and inverted receive is required. Never directly connect standard 5 V TTL or RS-232. A CH340/FTDI chip alone proves nothing about cable compatibility.

Other connectors

Some SPI Minis use a green 3-pin 5AS socket, separate from the white engine connector. Check the correct wiring diagram. No 5AS cable has been physically validated with Manager yet. Sources: James Portman and Andrew Revill.
16896:
Lucas 5AS remotes

Learning compatible Lucas PLIP remotes uses the same adapted 5AS diagnostic cable as the Immobiliser module: pins OBD 1/3 on 16-pin versions, suitable 0–12 V adaptation and inverted receive.

Cable adaptation

This is not a simple engine K-line repin: both signal lines and electrical adaptation are required. Versions with a green 3-pin socket require their own suitable cable.

Other families

Pektron SCU and Lucas 10AS are different systems. Suitable wiring and interfaces for Manager have not yet been verified. Never repin a KKL cable based on an assumption.

Important

433.92 MHz and 315 MHz are radio frequencies, not diagnostic cable types. Learning a 5AS remote may replace previously paired remotes. This module is not yet implemented and no programming is performed here. Sources: RoverMEMS, pscan and Andrew Revill.
